learning_outcomes.text: Know and distinguish between machining processes, types of machine tools, tools and fixtures used, motion patterns and reference systems of machine tools, their parameters, types of operations, and cutting tool geometry.
Know the programming of numerically controlled machine tools in the standardized ISO programming system.
Know and apply fixed machining cycles.
Know manufacturing engineering in general, as well as manufacturing systems and processes and their location in the productive context.

Know and distinguish between different manufacturing and process automation systems applied to industry, through the particular study of computer-aided design (CAD), manufacturing (CAM) and analysis (CAE) technologies, as well as flexible manufacturing systems (FMS).
Be able to use CAD/CAM applications.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION TO PROGRAMMING NUMERICALLY CONTROLLED MACHINE TOOLS

assessment_methods.method: Proposed project work or long programming problems during final exam

assessment_rules: The final exam, with a 60% weight, requires a minimum score of 3 points. Lab reports or lab exams account for 20% of the grade. Proposed project work or long programming problems during the final exam account for the remaining 20%. Incorrect answers in the final exam's test section will subtract points as indicated in the exam statement. Lab work will be assessed on correct handling of computer-aided manufacturing programs and the accuracy of submitted results. Project work and long problems will be assessed on the rigor and order followed in programming manufacturing operations, as well as the complexity and practical utility of the manufactured parts. Optionally, seminars may provide extra points.
